applies_why: The judge text decides a pressed link by treating Matthew 1:16's own grammar as admitting both readings, rather than weighing the competing chains by footing as K-C requires when chain witnesses are read together.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: "never verse by verse" — one reading bars using a single verse's ambiguity to leave a chain collision underdetermined; the other allows noting that the verse alone is open while still weighing the chains. I used the first reading.
why: The judge text labels Matthew 1:16 underdetermined solely because its grammar admits both readings, instead of weighing the pressed chain witnesses against each other by footing, so it violates K-C's chain-against-chain requirement.
